newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 23.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* AT&T Corp's fourth quarter income was helped by its new flat-rate calling plan, but earnings were below expectations because of higher costs from unpaid bills.
* Compaq Computer Corp's stock surged after the company's earnings exceeded Wall Street estimates.
* Conrail and CSX say they would be willing to meet with Norfolk Southern in what could be a break in the protracted takeover battle for East Coast rail dominance.
* A jury awards supermarket chain Food Lion more than $5.5 million in punitive damages in its case against Walt Disney Co's ABC.
* Bear Stearns Cos Inc second quarter profits rose 68 percent, and Dean Witter Discover & Co reports strong fourth quarter profits.
* USAir Group Inc fourth quarter earnings fall 55 percent.
* A judge rejects parts of a borrowing agreement negotiated by Marvel Entertainment Group Inc, possibly setting back Ronald Perelman's efforts to maintain control of the company.
* Treasury prices fell, and the 30-year bond yield rose to 6.82 percent from 6.78 percent.
* The share price of Pharmacia & Upjohn gets even cheaper after the resignation of Chief Executive John Zabriskie.
* Employees fighting a plan by the French government to cut jobs at Credit Foncier de France release the bank's president and other executives.
* A division of Johnson & Johnson moves the advertising account of its Nicotrol anti-smoking patch to Cordiant Plc's Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising from Omnicom Group's DDB Needham New York.
* Uno Restaurant Corp's Pizzeria Uno acknowledges its advertisements for "low-fat" pizzas were misleading and promises the Federal Trade Commission it will not to make such claims again.
* New York City created more jobs than its suburbs last year, the first time since 1980.
* DFS Group founder Charles Feeney has secretly given away more than $600 million of his fortune over the past 15 years.
* Enterprise Rent-a-Car Inc has become the giant of the car rental industry with estimated pretax profits of $500 million by carving out a special niche.
* The Federal Reserve's beige book survey showing that inflation remained under control could be a further indication that the central bank won't change interest rates at its February meeting.
* The Dow Jones industrial average drops 33.87 points, mainly from a plunge in shares of International Business Machines Corp.
